solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The final insult? Charge cut by 25 per cent eats funds

indicators.note: the shortened charge swallows the other piece, which sits inside it
cut signals that letters are taken away from the word for charge

parts.note: a toll is a charge for using a road or bridge
a quarter of the four-letter word for charge is one letter, here its last
capital is money or funds for investment

explanation.surface: A complaint about a fee that has been trimmed, yet still swallows your money: the last straw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut by 25 per cent' drops one of four letters, leaving TOL, which 'eats' the funds.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said of a last misfortune crowning a run of them, so a final insult fits.

clue.text: The best place to climb

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a spot is a place or location

explanation.surface: The ideal spot for climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is the tops is the very best, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Bird's swallowed her cigar

indicators.note: the word for bird takes the other word inside it

parts.note: a coot is a water bird; the 's means 'has'

explanation.surface: A bird has eaten a woman's cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a cigar with both ends cut square.

clue.text: Comfortable flats? Well, no

parts.note: plains are flat expanses of land
someone not well is ailing

explanation.surface: A query about whether some flats are comfortable to live in, answered no.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: the word break moves one letter to make the familiar phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy, untroubled progress is described as smooth and effortless, so it is comfortable.

clue.text: I'll attempt to hold butt in more?

indicators.note: the word for one who attempts holds the other inside

parts.note: a trier is one who will attempt things
a butt is the end of something, such as a cigarette

explanation.surface: Someone resolving to hold in a cigarette butt.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'more in', more fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in means being fashionable, so more in is more fashionable.

clue.text: Cat has hair regularly stuck in part of throat

indicators.note: the selected letters are put inside the word for a cat

parts.note: a lynx is a wild cat

indicators.note: takes every other letter of the word hair

explanation.surface: A cat has a hairball caught in its throat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes A and R from hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The voice box is the organ in the upper windpipe, a part of the throat.

clue.text: Chasing opponents, one may initially feel dizzy

indicators.note: the following pieces chase, that is come after, the opponents

parts.note: in bridge South and West sit as opponents of each other's partners, S and W being on rival sides
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the word may

explanation.surface: A runner pursuing rivals might start to feel giddy.
explanation.walkthrough: SW are bridge players on opposite sides; 'Chasing' puts I and M after them.
explanation.definitionFit: When your head swims you feel giddy and unsteady, an idiomatic sense of the verb.

clue.text: Time to grab extremely short pipe

indicators.note: the word for time grabs the letters inside it

parts.note: a while is a period of time

indicators.note: takes the outer letters of short

explanation.surface: Time to snatch a quick pipe smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin whistle is a small wind instrument, a simple pipe.

clue.text: Way sailor is controlling

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner
a rating is a non-commissioned sailor in the Navy

explanation.surface: A sailor's manner of exercising command.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderating means presiding over or restraining, ways of controlling.

clue.text: About to chase rare bird, one seeing another nest?

indicators.note: the word for about comes after, chasing, the other pieces

parts.note: pie is a rare, old name for the magpie
a dater is someone seeing, that is going out with, another person
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone chasing a rare bird and spotting another one's nest, like a twitcher.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'nest' is a human one: a small second home.
explanation.definitionFit: A small flat or house kept for occasional stays is a home or nest away from home, a playful extension.

clue.text: Child's put in new class

indicators.note: the letter for new is placed inside the word for a child

parts.note: a kid is a child; the 's stands for 'has'

explanation.surface: A pupil has been moved into a fresh class at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Kind means sort or type, the same as a class of things.

clue.text: Favour a foreigner's pronunciation of 'Dionysiac'

indicators.note: says the clue words are spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: favour is back, a is an, a foreigner is an alien: back an alien

explanation.surface: Supporting a foreigner's way of saying the word Dionysiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Dionysus is the Greek name of the wine god Bacchus, so both adjectives describe drunken revelry.

clue.text: Sort of dress that's good to have

parts.note: to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: A frock described as a good one to own.
explanation.definitionFit: A long formal frock, as for a ball, is one particular kind of dress.

clue.text: Racecourse jockey not scared

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre or shift about, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A rider at the track who shows no fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jockey' looks like the rider but is a verb telling us to rearrange NOTSCARED.
explanation.definitionFit: This town in Yorkshire, England, hosts a famous horse-racing venue where the St Leger is run.

clue.text: Endless fuel for ranches as standard?

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped

parts.note: coal is a fuel
to can mean for, as in 'a toast to the host'
ranches are farms

explanation.surface: A query whether endless fuel for ranches is the norm.
explanation.definitionFit: A heraldic banner, or standard, displays the family shield and its devices.

clue.text: Furious with remote uni having curtailed play

parts.note: the Open University, OU, teaches students remotely by distance learning

indicators.note: cut short at the tail, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a tragedy is a kind of play

explanation.surface: Someone angry that a distance-learning university cut its drama production short.
explanation.definitionFit: Being outraged is being furiously angry, a near synonym.

clue.text: Stress I had to leave crash

indicators.note: the letters for I had go out of the word for crash

parts.note: a crash is an accident
ID is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone recounting that a car crash left them under stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Accent is emphasis placed on a syllable, which is stress in speech.

clue.text: Very short river heading for this county

parts.note: so means very

indicators.note: the river name loses its last letter

parts.note: the Mersey is a river in north-west England

indicators.note: takes the first letter of this

explanation.surface: A short river flows toward a county.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is a county in south-west England, an example of the category.

clue.text: Drink very quietly hidden in hat

indicators.note: the musical marking goes inside the word for hat

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quietly

explanation.surface: A secret drink stashed in someone's hat and sipped on the quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipple is an alcoholic drink, especially one habitually taken.

clue.text: Effect of a protocol

parts.note: per means a or each, as in miles per hour
form is correct procedure or etiquette, a protocol

explanation.surface: A consequence of following an agreed protocol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Effect' is a verb, to carry out.
explanation.definitionFit: To effect something is to carry it out, which is to execute or do it.

clue.text: The same people present

parts.note: do, short for ditto, means the same again
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: The same group of people are here in attendance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like an adjective (here) but is a noun, a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift, as a present is.

clue.text: Perfume from nettle?

definitions.meaning: scented smoke from burning resin or sticks
to nettle is to annoy or anger, a verb

explanation.surface: Asking whether a scent can be made from a stinging weed.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is aromatic smoke; the verb, stressed on the second syllable, means enrage.

clue.text: What pigeon goes across to pull flying lemur

indicators.note: the pigeon's call stretches across the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a pigeon's call is coo
to lug is to pull or drag

explanation.surface: A pigeon flies over to drag away a gliding lemur.
explanation.definitionFit: The colugo, a gliding mammal of South-East Asia, is commonly known by this other name.

clue.text: Miles and Oleg cut short country dance

parts.note: miles away means far

indicators.note: the name loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Two men, Miles and Oleg, have their folk dance stopped early.
explanation.walkthrough: Miles looks like a name but is the distance.
explanation.definitionFit: The farandole is a lively Provençal folk dance done in a chain.

clue.text: Norman is one into Cheddar Cheese

indicators.note: the letters run into the words that follow, concealed across them

explanation.surface: A man called Norman is keen on Cheddar cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman is not a man: the definition is architectural.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norman style of building used round-headed curved openings, so a Norman one is an example.

clue.text: Dry, although with river running through

indicators.note: the river letter runs through the middle of the other word

parts.note: but and although can both introduce a contrast

explanation.surface: A dry landscape even though a river flows through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brut is the term for very dry champagne or sparkling wine.

clue.text: While talking, fold fleece

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a ruck is a crease or fold in cloth

explanation.surface: Talking while folding a fleece garment.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound match depends on accent: in some northern English speech the two words rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to swindle them, which is one sense of the verb.

clue.text: I doubt drunk is not given case of rum

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are put inside a casing formed by the word for rum

parts.note: rum and queer both mean odd

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters reel about into a new order

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubting that a drunk is not given some rum.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who doubts things, as the speaker of I doubt does, is a querier or sceptic.

clue.text: Heading off by reversing truck

indicators.note: the remaining letters are read backwards
the first letter is removed

parts.note: in arithmetic, three by four is three times four

explanation.surface: Pull off the road by backing up a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is the multiplication sense; drop the T and reverse IMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for semi-trailer, an articulated lorry or truck.

clue.text: Satisfied nursing home has good company

indicators.note: the word for satisfied holds the others as if cradling them

parts.note: content means satisfied
in means at home

explanation.surface: A care home with a good, satisfied workforce.
explanation.definitionFit: A contingent is a group or body of people, like a company of soldiers.
